facts.statement: The genus Pterorhynchus was named in 2002 by Stephen Czerkas and Ji Qiang.
facts.quote: The genus was named in 2002 by Stephen Czerkas and Ji Qiang.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Pterorhynchus wellnhoferi.
facts.quote: The type species is Pterorhynchus wellnhoferi.

facts.statement: The genus name means "wing snout" and refers to the tall crest on the animal's head.
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from Greek pteron, "wing" and rhynchos, "snout", in reference to the tall crest on the head.

facts.statement: The specific name wellnhoferi honors the German pterosaur researcher Peter Wellnhofer.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the German pterosaur researcher Peter Wellnhofer.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found in Chifeng within the Daohugou Beds.
facts.quote: It was found in Chifeng in the Daohugou Beds.

facts.statement: Ji assigned Pterorhynchus to the Yanliao Biota of the Haifanggou Formation during the Callovian stage.
facts.quote: According to Ji Pterorhynchus belongs to the Yanliao Biota from the Haifanggou Formation of the Callovian

facts.statement: Lü Junchang in 2007 suggested the animal lived in the later Tiaojishan Formation of the same stage.
facts.quote: Lü Junchang in 2007 ascribed it to the somewhat later Tiaojishan Formation of the same stage.

facts.statement: Pterorhynchus lived between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago during the Callovian.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Callovian (165.3 to 161.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: The specimen preserved the wing membrane, hair-like structures, a long tail vane, and a head crest with a bony base and large keratin extension.
facts.quote: These included the wing membrane, hair-like structures, a long version of the vane found at the end of "rhamphorhynchoid" tails, and a head crest with both a low bony base and a large keratin extension

facts.statement: A head crest is an unusual feature for basal pterosaurs, which rarely show such structures in fossils.
facts.quote: the latter feature is unusual in "rhamphorhynchoids" (i.e., basal pterosaurs), the fossils of which do not often show head crests.

facts.statement: The crest covered the posterior two-thirds of the head and was reinforced by a dozen parallel ridges.
facts.quote: The crest covered the posterior two thirds of the head, showed the presence of minute oval scales and was reinforced by a dozen ridges running parallel to the rounded trailing edge.

facts.statement: A vertical pattern at the base of the crest was interpreted as original camouflage coloration.
facts.quote: At the base, a vertical pattern was visible, interpreted as corresponding to the original camouflage colour patterning.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested the head crest had a primarily aerodynamic function.
facts.quote: The describers ascribed a primarily aerodynamic function to the crest, which is reflected in the genus name.

facts.statement: The fibers were described as pinnate, resembling the base of bird down feathers, and were seen as corresponding to Stage II in feather evolution.
facts.quote: These were described as pinnate, with many strands arising from a single base (similar to the calamus of the down feathers in birds), and seen as corresponding to the hypothetical Stage II in the evolution of feathers.

facts.statement: The presence of these fibers suggests that pterosaur pycnofibers and dinosaur feathers were homologous.
facts.quote: This would suggest that pterosaur pycnofibres and dinosaur feathers were homologous.

facts.statement: Czerkas and Ji originally assigned Pterorhynchus to the family Rhamphorhynchidae.
facts.quote: In their description of Pterorhynchus, Czerka and Ji assigned it to the Rhamphorhynchidae.

facts.statement: A 2014 analysis by Andres and colleagues found Pterorhynchus to be a close relative of wukongopterids and therefore closer to pterodactyloid pterosaurs.
facts.quote: A large phylogenetic analysis performed by Brian Andres and colleagues in 2014 found that Pterorhynchus was actually a close relative of the similar-looking wukongopterids, and therefore a closer relative of pterodactyloid pterosaurs.

facts.statement: Andres and colleagues assigned Pterorhynchus to the group Darwinoptera.
facts.quote: Andres and colleagues assigned both the wukongopterids and Pterorhynchus to the group Darwinoptera.

facts.statement: Pterorhynchus belongs to the suborder Rhamphorhynchoidea.
facts.quote: subordo: Rhamphorhynchoidea

facts.statement: Pterorhynchus is part of the unranked family Darwinoptera.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Darwinoptera

facts.statement: The parent group of Pterorhynchus is Rhamphorhynchinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Rhamphorhynchinae

facts.statement: Pterorhynchus is classified in the family Rhamphorhynchidae.
facts.quote: Family: Rhamphorhynchidae

rejected.quote: The only known specimen had an elongated skull 11.8 cm long, a long tail, and a wingspan of about 85 cm.

rejected.quote: Hair-like pycnofibers covered the body, and tiny tufts of fibers also covered portions of the wing membrane.
